Hi Alex 	6 thanks for the great questions and for the time today. Quick recap and next steps below. I'm looping in Ben (SE) and Dev (Security/Infra) to provide detail and attachments.

Recap / answers at a high level:
- PII handling: Redwood does not persist customer prompt or response content by default in hosted mode. Customers can opt into longer retention for debugging; retention windows are configurable per account. We also provide a policy-driven scrub/filter option that can mask common PII patterns before persistence.
- Data residency: requests are routed to region-specific clusters according to the account region. We support EU-only routing for EU-marked data and offer contracts for strict residency. Model failover to other regions only occurs under explicit cross-region fallback policies customers opt into.
- Access controls (RBAC): we provide role-based roles (Admin, Developer, Auditor, Support) with least-privilege defaults. Admins can create scoped API keys and service accounts.
- Support / break-glass: emergency support access is gated: access requests require an auditable JIRA ticket + approval and are time-limited. All break-glass sessions are logged and surfaced in the audit trail.
- Logging & audit: we expose request-level metadata (timestamps, model, prompt hash) and optional full request/response logs for customers who enable retention. Logs can be exported via secure transfer (S3) and retained per the contract.

Attachments I'm adding here for your review: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary) and an example access-controls-matrix (spreadsheet). Ben / Dev: can you add any technical caveats about PII detection, retention defaults, and exactly what's in the log export?

Hi Alex 	6 quick technical notes to supplement Marissa's summary:

PII detection & masking:
- We offer configurable regex-based and ML-based PII scrubbing hooks that run pre-ingest in the control plane. Customers can opt to apply scrubbing at the request level; we also surface a prompt-hash instead of raw prompt by default in metadata.
- For debugging, customers can enable full content retention for a scoped set of API keys; by default this is off.

Retention & log exports:
- Default retention for request traces (metadata only) is 30 days in hosted by default. Log exports (full request/response) are available and can be pushed to a customer S3 bucket; retention is contract-configurable (30/90/365 days).

RBAC & support access:
- Roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Read-only/Auditor, Support-Handler (limited).
- Least privilege: role templates and org-level policies (e.g., restrict model deployment, restrict billing views).
- Break-glass workflow: support opens an emergency request in our ticketing system; request must be approved by two on-call engineers and is timeboxed. All session recordings and steps are stored in the audit log and tied to the ticket ID.

Auditing:
- Audit trail covers: who (internal user id/email), when (UTC timestamp), what action (API key creation, access via break-glass, data export), and evidence (ticket id, session id). We provide these as JSONL logs for ingestion into SIEMs.

Caveats / notes:
- If you require FIPS/HSM-backed key storage for keys used to encrypt log exports, that's available under our Private deployment offering (we can scope in the contract).
- Cross-region fallback is only enabled with an explicit policy; by default we will not route EU-tagged traffic outside EU clusters.

Happy to walk through the access-controls-matrix on the call. Marissa — I can join Tue 8 Jun 10am PT.
